correctness.rationale: The reduced Markov state (k,A) has exact ordinary-ordinary transition rate k(k-1)/2 and individual impurity rate k*lambda_i. Every event removes 2 vertices; the k=1 terminal rule is a rate-proportional impurity choice or ordinary vacancy. Holding-time exposure E=integral k dt until k<=ceil(log n)^2 has conditional mean sum 2/(k-1+2sum active rates)=log(n/K)+o(1), and variance O(1/K); only r one-step changes affect mesh O(1/K). Independent exponential hazard thresholds force bulk survival Bernoulli(e^-c_i) as E/log n->1. A harmonic union bound O(loglog n/log n) excludes captures at 2<=k<=K; remaining parity completes the finite state law and hence TV convergence. For r=2 even n, no impurity ever matched is product of ordinary edge selection probabilities at k=2j, giving exact finite product and limiting exp(-(c1+c2)). Independent freshly implemented exact rational labeled-edge recursion equaled reduced Markov recursion in 10 cases (r=2,3) and directly verified even-n product in tested cases; unrestricted limit rests on the exposure/threshold proof.

value.rationale: The 1/log n impurity rate is the mathematically natural transition scale because cumulative ordinary-vertex exposure is logarithmic. The sharp labeled Poisson-binomial survival and parity-dependent terminal selection determine more than mean coverage or bulk jamming fraction, and the r=2 finite product is an exact useful observable.

final_claim: For fixed r>=2 impurities and c_i>0 on a dense ordinary clique, impurity-edge attempt rates c_i/log n yield independent Bernoulli bulk survivors p_i=e^{-c_i}; terminal parity forces at most one size-biased deletion and a complete labeled total-variation jamming law along parity subsequences. For r=2 even n, probability of two uncovered vertices has exact product over odd k involving lambda1+lambda2.
limitations: Fixed r and positive c_i; no growing impurity count, physical adsorption time, or growing-rate uniform error bound.
Full weighted-greedy primary literature still needs priority reconciliation.
